blocks.text: Evidence is the data captured when sensitive information is discovered during an on-premises scan. Evidence collection is a feature in DSPM to capture and store evidence of sensitive information found during on-premises scanning. The data snippets are stored directly in your organization's cloud storage (e.g., AWS S3 bucket) and are not stored in the Zscaler infrastructure, maintaining compliance with data privacy and security.
Evidence configuration is linked to specific on-premises data centers. Sensitive data detected by the on-premises scanner is uploaded to the configured cloud storage via DSPM.
You can choose how to provision the cloud storage:

blocks.item: Zscaler Managed: DSPM automatically creates and manages a storage bucket in your cloud account. This is the recommended option for a simple setup.
Custom: You provide an existing S3 bucket that is already configured in your organization's cloud account.

blocks.text: Configuring evidence settings provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Store sensitive data on your cloud infrastructure.
Protect data with end-to-end encryption throughout the entire workflow, from scanning to storage.
Route the evidence data through the existing DSPM service connection and eliminate the need to open the on-premises scanner network to external cloud storage IP addresses.
Provide security analysts with proof of sensitive data discovery to expedite remediation.
Centralize evidence rules for multiple on-premises data centers in a single view.

blocks.text: On the Evidence Settings page (Data Security > DSPM > Evidence Settings), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Search for specific rules using the rule name.
Modify the table and its columns.
Add a new evidence rule.
View the list of configured evidence rules. For each rule, you can view the following details:
Rule Name: The name assigned to the evidence rule during configuration.
Evidence Rule Details
For each evidence rule, you can view the following details:
Action menu to edit, validate, or delete the evidence rule configuration.
Evidence:
Rule Name: The name assigned to the evidence rule during configuration.
Cloud Type: The public cloud provider hosting the evidence storage.
S3 Bucket Name (or equivalent): The name of the storage bucket or container where the evidence snippets are stored.
Storage Type: Indicates if the storage is Zscaler managed (provisioned by DSPM) or a custom (provided by the customer).
S3 Bucket Account ID: The identifier of the cloud account where the evidence storage bucket is located.
KMS Key ARN (Custom Storage): The identifier for your encryption key, ensuring data at rest is protected by your organization's security policies.
Data Centers: The list of data centers associated with this rule. Any scanner assigned to these data centers uses this rule for evidence uploads.

IAM Role: The IAM role (e.g., z-dspm-evidence-role) created in your cloud environment. This role grants the scanner permission to upload findings and the Zscaler Admin Console permission to read them.
Download Template:
CloudFormation: Download CloudFormation template to automate the provisioning of the required IAM roles and policies.
Terraform: Download Terraform template for managing your infrastructure configuration.
Datastore: The type of data store associated with the evidence rule.
Cloud: The public cloud provider hosting the evidence storage.
Storage Type: Indicates whether the storage is Zscaler managed or a custom (provided by the customer).
Connection Status: The validation status (Success, Failed, Pending) of the evidence rule.
Error: The error message indicating why the evidence rule validation failed.
Enable/Disable: Indicates whether the evidence rule is active. Toggle to enable or disable the rule.
Added By: The user who added the evidence rule.
Added On: The date and time the evidence rule was added.
Sort the column data.
Use the Actions icon to edit, validate, or delete the rule configuration.
